description:
Health coverage, disability, nativity and income by race — the tables the Census Bureau does not publish for block groups, which is why this chunk has no block-group twin. The uninsured share and the share with a disability ([B27001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B27001), [B18101](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B18101)), the foreign-born share ([B05002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B05002)), the group-quarters population ([B26001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B26001)), median household income for Black, non-Hispanic White, Asian and Hispanic householders ([B19013B](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013B), [B19013H](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013H), [B19013D](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013D), [B19013I](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013I)), and the poverty rate of the Black alone population ([B17020B](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B17020B)).

Curated indicators for all **441** congressional districts of the 119th Congress in the United States, Puerto Rico and the island areas, from the U.S. Census Bureau's [American Community Survey](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs.html) **2020–2024 5-year estimates** (`acsdt5y2024`, the table-based [Summary File](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/2024/table-based-SF/data/5YRData/)). The Census Bureau calls the ACS "the premier source of detailed information about the nation's people and housing". The Bureau also publishes 1-year estimates at this geography; the 5-year release is used throughout this catalog so every geography in it is the same vintage and directly comparable.

Every estimate ships with its margin of error — `<column>_moe`, at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes — and the headline statistics also carry a coefficient of variation (`<column>_cv` = `moe / 1.645 / estimate`) so small-area noise can be flagged rather than mapped as if certain. Derived percentages propagate error with the Census Bureau's own formulas from [ACS Accuracy of the Data](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/tech_docs/accuracy/MultiyearACSAccuracyofData2024.pdf): sums add in quadrature, proportions use the subset formula with the ratio formula as fallback. ACS jam values for suppressed or unestimable cells are NULL here, never numbers, and medians are published as the Bureau publishes them — a median cannot be aggregated to a larger area. Each column's description names its ACS table, its exact universe, and the lines summed to make it.

Districts are equal-population by construction — 546,488 to 1,021,191 people across the 435 voting districts, 771,301 at the median of all 437 rows with data (measured) — so the distribution of every rate here is far tighter than at any other geography, and the map styles' class breaks are measured accordingly. These are the districts of the **119th Congress** ([the vintage this ACS release tabulates](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/geography-acs/geography-boundaries-by-year/2024.html)); district numbers are not stable across congresses, so do not join these GEOIDs to an earlier congress's districts of the same number. All four race-iteration medians are published for 436 or 437 of the 441 rows — only `median_hh_income_asian` loses a fifth district (**1.13%** NULL) — which makes this the finest geography in the catalog where a race-and-income comparison is close to complete. Three districts carry a `median_hh_income_black_cv` above 0.40 (maximum 0.480, measured).

Geometries are the Census Bureau's [2024 cartographic boundary files](https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/cartographic-boundary.html) for congressional districts of the 119th Congress (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), reprojected to EPSG:4326 and joined on `GEOID`. Cartographic rather than TIGER/Line because TIGER extends census geographies into open water while the cartographic files clip to the shoreline, which is what a choropleth wants. The file is `cb_2024_us_cd119_500k` — `CDSESSN = '119'` on all 441 features — matching the congress this release tabulates.

The join is driven by geometry, so a geography with 2024 boundaries but no ACS tabulation keeps its row with NULL values instead of disappearing: 4 delegate districts (American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, the U.S. Virgin Islands) in the island areas, which have cartographic boundaries but no ACS 5-year estimates because the Island Areas run a separate decennial-only program. In the other direction, three ACS district rows have no polygon and so no row here: `09ZZ`, `17ZZ` and `33ZZ`, the water-only pseudo-districts Connecticut, Illinois and New Hampshire contribute to the tabulation, each with population 0. Keeping these rows means a national map has no holes and a consumer can see the absence; dropping them would make "every US geography" quietly mean something narrower.

This is one themed chunk of six at this geography. The other themes are [Income & Poverty](../cd-income/collection.json), [People & Education](../cd-people/collection.json), [Housing & Rent](../cd-housing/collection.json) and [Commuting & Connectivity](../cd-connectivity/collection.json), split that way so a consumer who wants one theme reads one file. Chunks at the same geography hold the same rows and the same geometry, so they join 1:1 on `geoid`. A sixth collection, [All Indicators](../congressional-districts/collection.json), carries all 112 columns on the same rows in one wide table — at this many features width costs little, so take that one if a question crosses themes. A district nests in a state, so `substr(geoid, 1, 2)` reaches the state row; nothing finer joins by prefix, because district boundaries follow 2020 census blocks rather than counties or tracts. Every other geography in this catalog is organized the same way — [block groups](../../block-groups/catalog.json), [census tracts](../../tracts/catalog.json), [counties](../../counties/catalog.json), [states](../../states/catalog.json), [ZCTAs](../../zctas/catalog.json) and [places and CDPs](../../places/catalog.json) — and the [blocks](../../blocks/collection.json) collection carries 2020 Decennial counts, a different survey and vintage rather than a finer version of these numbers.

The PMTiles archive carries the same columns as the GeoParquet, minus the `*_moe` columns, and at every zoom the tiles are the real census geographies — there are few enough features here to draw them all at a national zoom, so this archive needs none of the coarser-geography coarse-zoom bands the catalog's finer collections carry. Built with [tylertoo](https://github.com/geoparquet-io/tylertoo). Statistics still come from the GeoParquet: margins of error are not in the tiles.

This is a mirror — [data.census.gov](https://data.census.gov/) is authoritative, and nothing here is an official Census Bureau product. The exact upstream files this collection was built from are published as `source` assets, linked at their original census.gov URLs, so the original is always one click away; the Bureau's own documentation is linked alongside them. Read the collection's [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) before querying: it carries the schema, the join keys, the NULL-rate story and tested queries against the published URLs.

table:columns.name: geoid
table:columns.description: 4-character congressional district GEOID — state FIPS (2) + district (2), e.g. `0612` for California's 12th. `substr(geoid, 1, 2)` is the state FIPS code. At-large states use district `00` (AK, DE, ND, SD, VT, WY) and the non-voting delegate districts use `98` (`1198` District of Columbia, `7298` Puerto Rico, plus the four island areas). Districts of the **119th Congress**, which is the vintage the ACS 2020–2024 5-year release tabulates: matches `GEOID` in the `cb_2024_us_cd119_500k` cartographic boundary file (`CDSESSN = '119'` on every feature) and the ACS `5001900US` prefix, whose `19` is the congress number, is stripped. District numbers are not stable across congresses, so a `geoid` here does not join to a 118th-Congress district of the same number.

table:columns.name: name
table:columns.description: `NAMELSAD` from the cartographic boundary congressional district file plus the state name from the state file — "Congressional District 12, California", "Delegate District (at Large), District of Columbia".

table:columns.name: state
table:columns.description: Two-letter USPS state or territory code (`MO`, `PR`, `GU`). Carried on every collection from the `STATEFP → USPS` lookup embedded in `tools/specs.py` rather than read off the boundary files, because the 2024 cartographic boundary block-group file has no `STUSPS` column while the tract, county and state files do.

table:columns.name: population
table:columns.description: Total population. Universe: total population. The single line of [B01003](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B01003) (Total Population), published as an integer. Carried on every ACS collection so a rate can be weighted or sanity-checked without a second download. NULL on 0.91% of districts — the four island-area delegate districts (American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, the U.S. Virgin Islands), which have 2024 boundaries but no ACS 5-year estimates. Every other column in this collection is NULL on the same four rows and nowhere else.

table:columns.name: population_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `population` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Component margins add in quadrature — `sqrt(Σ moe²)` — which is the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a sum. NULL when every component is a jam value.

table:columns.name: aland_sqkm
table:columns.description: Land area in square kilometres, rounded to 3 decimals. `ALAND / 1e6` from the cartographic boundary file. Land only: water area is excluded, which is what makes it the right denominator for population density.

table:columns.name: pop_density
table:columns.description: People per square kilometre of land area, rounded to 1 decimal: `population / aland_sqkm`. NULL where `ALAND` is 0 or `population` is NULL.

table:columns.name: pct_uninsured
table:columns.description: Percent of the civilian noninstitutionalized population with no health insurance coverage. Universe: civilian noninstitutionalized population — people on active duty and people in institutions are outside it. The "No health insurance coverage" lines of [B27001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B27001) over line 1, resolved from the table shells by label (9 age groups × 2 sexes = 18 lines for this vintage) rather than hardcoded. Not published for block groups, which is why there is no block-group twin of this collection.

table:columns.name: pct_uninsured_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_uninsured` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_uninsured_cv
table:columns.description: Coefficient of variation for `pct_uninsured`: `moe / 1.645 / estimate`, rounded to 3 decimals — the standard error as a fraction of the estimate, with 1.645 converting the published 90% margin back to a standard error. A rule of thumb: under 0.12 reliable, 0.12–0.40 use with caution, over 0.40 unreliable. NULL when the estimate is NULL or 0, or the margin of error is NULL. Published on the headline statistics so a map can grey out the geographies whose value is swamped by its own error instead of drawing them as if certain.

table:columns.name: pct_with_disability
table:columns.description: Percent of the civilian noninstitutionalized population with a disability, as the ACS's six-question sequence defines it (hearing, vision, cognitive, ambulatory, self-care, independent living). Universe: civilian noninstitutionalized population. The "With a disability" lines of [B18101](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B18101) over line 1, resolved from the shells by label (6 age groups × 2 sexes = 12 lines for this vintage).

table:columns.name: pct_with_disability_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_with_disability` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Propagated with the Census Bureau's proportion formula, `sqrt(moe_num² − p²·moe_den²) / den`, falling back to the ratio formula (`+` instead of `−`) when the radicand goes negative because the numerator is not a true subset of the denominator. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: pct_foreign_born
table:columns.description: Percent of the population that is foreign-born — anyone not a U.S. citizen at birth, naturalized citizens included. Universe: total population. Line 13 ("Foreign-born") over line 1 of [B05002](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B05002) (Place of Birth by Nativity and Citizenship Status). People born abroad to American parents (line 12) are native-born and are not in this share.

table:columns.name: pct_foreign_born_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `pct_foreign_born` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Multiplied by 100 to match the percentage, rounded to 2 decimals, and NULL rather than guessed when an input margin is NULL or the denominator is 0.

table:columns.name: group_quarters_pop
table:columns.description: Population living in group quarters — correctional facilities, nursing facilities, college and university housing, military quarters, group homes, shelters. Universe: population in group quarters. Line 1 of [B26001](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B26001), published as an integer. A large value next to a small household population usually explains an odd median: a prison or a dorm dominates the geography.

table:columns.name: group_quarters_pop_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `group_quarters_pop` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Component margins add in quadrature — `sqrt(Σ moe²)` — which is the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a sum. NULL when every component is a jam value.

table:columns.name: median_hh_income_black
table:columns.description: Median household income in the past 12 months (2024 inflation-adjusted dollars) for households whose householder is Black or African American alone. Universe: households with a householder who is Black or African American alone. Line 1 of [B19013B](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013B), the B race iteration of [B19013](https://data.census.gov/table/ACSDT5Y2024.B19013). Classified by the householder's race, not by every member's.

table:columns.name: median_hh_income_black_moe
table:columns.description: Margin of error for `median_hh_income_black` at the 90% confidence level, the level the Census Bureau publishes. Published as the Census Bureau publishes it for this line. A median's margin cannot be recomputed from a distribution, so it is passed through untouched.

table:columns.name: median_hh_income_black_cv
table:columns.description: Coefficient of variation for `median_hh_income_black`: `moe / 1.645 / estimate`, rounded to 3 decimals — the standard error as a fraction of the estimate, with 1.645 converting the published 90% margin back to a standard error. NULL on 1.13% of districts: the four island-area delegate districts plus one district with no published Asian-householder median.

Universe: Black or African American alone population for whom poverty status is determined — a race-specific universe, so this is not comparable to `pct_below_poverty`'s denominator. table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: Boundary polygon (Polygon or MultiPolygon), WKB-encoded, in EPSG:4326 / OGC:CRS84 — the GeoParquet default CRS, written as an omitted `crs` key. From the Census Bureau's 2024 cartographic boundary congressional district file (GENZ2024, 1:500,000), which clips to the shoreline — TIGER/Line would extend the congressional district into open water. Generalized for mapping and point-in-polygon work, not for legal-boundary or precise-area work.

table:columns.name: bbox
table:columns.type: struct<xmin: double, ymin: double, xmax: double, ymax: double>
table:columns.description: GeoParquet 1.1 covering struct (`xmin`, `ymin`, `xmax`, `ymax`) for the row's geometry, with row-group statistics, so a spatial filter can skip most of the file over the network. Written by geoparquet-io, not by the Census Bureau.

styles/default.title: People without health insurance
styles/default.description: Share of the civilian non-institutionalized population with no health insurance coverage, pale yellow to deep red. Measured over all 437 districts with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 5%/6.5%/8.5%/11%/14%, which fall at the 22nd/43rd/59th/80th/91st percentile of the national distribution.

styles/disability.title: People with a disability
styles/disability.description: Share of the civilian non-institutionalized population reporting a disability, pale pink to deep magenta. Measured over all 437 districts with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 11%/12%/14%/15%/17%, which fall at the 22nd/34th/60th/73rd/91st percentile of the national distribution.

styles/foreign-born.title: Foreign-born residents
styles/foreign-born.description: Share of residents born outside the United States, pale green to deep blue. Measured over all 437 districts with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at 5%/8%/14%/22%/32%, which fall at the 20th/39th/61st/78th/91st percentile of the national distribution.

styles/income-black-households.title: Median income, Black households
styles/income-black-households.description: Median household income for Black or African American householders (ACS table B19013B), cividis navy (low) to gold (high). Measured over all 437 districts with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at $55k/$70k/$80k/$95k/$115k, which fall at the 41st/72nd/83rd/93rd/98th percentile of the national distribution. Shares its breaks and ramp with the white non-Hispanic style, so switching between the two shows the gap directly; the Census publishes this estimate only where the district's Black household count supports one. 0.69% of districts have a coefficient of variation above 0.3; this style does not fade them, so read median_hh_income_black_moe in the GeoParquet before drawing a conclusion from any single district.

styles/income-white-households.title: Median income, white non-Hispanic households
styles/income-white-households.description: Median household income for white, non-Hispanic householders (ACS table B19013H), on the same scale as the Black-household style. Measured over all 437 districts with a published value: 6 classes with breaks at $55k/$70k/$80k/$95k/$115k, which fall at the 0th/12th/38th/60th/85th percentile of the national distribution. Same breaks, ramp and opacity rule as the Black-household style — neither fades its noisy estimates, because fading only one of the pair would make the gap look like a difference in confidence.

source-cartographic-boundaries.title: 2024 cartographic boundary file — congressional districts of the 119th Congress (1:500,000, national)

Only the join key, the name parts and the land-area field are kept; reprojected from NAD83 to EPSG:4326 with ogr2ogr. `CDSESSN = '119'` on every feature, matching the congress this ACS release tabulates. Served by census.gov.

doc-geo-tallies.title: 2020 Census national geographic entity tallies
doc-geo-tallies.description: The published count of every geographic entity type, which this collection's row count is checked against: 33,791 ZCTAs (33,642 US + 132 Puerto Rico + 17 island areas), 19,734 incorporated places and 12,454 census designated places, 441 congressional districts (436 US including the DC delegate + 1 Puerto Rico + 4 island areas). Index page: https://www.census.gov/geographies/reference-files/time-series/geo/tallies.html.

doc-cd119.title: Congressional Districts of the 119th Congress — Census Bureau
doc-cd119.description: The Bureau's page for the district plans this collection maps. The vintage is confirmed by https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/geography-acs/geography-boundaries-by-year/2024.html, which lists "Congressional District, Delegate District DC, Resident Commissioner District PR" with a vintage of "119th Congress of the United States" for the 2024 ACS.

doc-acs-handbook.title: Understanding and Using American Community Survey Data — Census Bureau handbooks
doc-acs-handbook.description: The Bureau's own guidance on what ACS estimates can and cannot support: 1-year versus 5-year releases, margins of error, comparing across vintages, and small-area reliability. Read it before drawing a conclusion from a single block group.

doc-acs-accuracy.title: ACS Accuracy of the Data (2024, multiyear estimates)
doc-acs-accuracy.description: The source of every margin-of-error formula this build applies: quadrature for sums, the proportion formula and its ratio fallback for percentages, and the definition of the published 90% confidence level.

doc-acs-subject-definitions.title: ACS 2024 Subject Definitions
doc-acs-subject-definitions.description: The Census Bureau's definitions of the concepts behind these columns — household, householder, gross rent, poverty status determined, group quarters, means of transportation to work, disability. Where a column description here says what a universe is, this is the document it is saying it from.

doc-geo-glossary.title: Census Bureau geography program glossary
doc-geo-glossary.description: Definitions of the geographies and the identifiers used here — block, block group, tract, county equivalent, GEOID, and what nests inside what.
